title: 'I Couldn't Save Them All': Oregon Dad Crawled Through Window to Stop Elementary School Shooter
snippet: Kaylub Giamanco, a 36-year-old father of two, took swift action to neutralize a teenage gunman at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, saving countless lives.
content:
A Bend, Oregon father who army-crawled through a shattered window to stop a teenage gunman at his daughters' elementary school has been identified, as officials and community members hail his courage during a deadly tragedy.

Kaylub Giamanco, 36, stepped in Friday to confront and fatally shoot a 16-year-old attacker at Silver Rail Elementary School, bringing an end to a rampage that claimed the lives of three children and a teacher. Two others—a student and another teacher—remain critically injured in the hospital.

'He Army-Crawled Through the Window'

Giamanco’s mother, Kenda Freeman, shared the harrowing details of her son's actions. After noticing something suspicious outside the school, Giamanco pulled his vehicle onto the lawn, armed himself, and entered the building through a shot-out window.

"Kaylub knew something was not right, so he pulled up onto the grass, grabbed his gun and basically stalked the gunman back into the school," Freeman said. "He crawled through a window that the gunman had shot out. He army-crawled through the window."

Shortly after neutralizing the threat, Giamanco called his mother in distress. "I told him he was a hero, he did what he had to do, and that I was proud of him... and he saved a lot of lives," Freeman recalled. "And he said, 'Mom, I couldn't save them all.'"

Teachers and First Responders Praised

Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz commended Giamanco alongside a brave classroom teacher who attempted to disarm the attacker prior to Giamanco's intervention. According to police, the teacher threw her cellphone at the gunman, tackled him, and fought to wrest the firearm away.

"She was not injured in that incident, but she almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed," Chief Krantz said.

Public figures across the state and nation weighed in on the heroism displayed during the crisis. President Trump called Giamanco a "great hero" who "took care of business," while Oregon Governor Tina Kotek expressed gratitude for the bystander's intervention while acknowledging the immense "heavy emotional burden" of the ordeal.

Community Mourns Amid Ongoing Investigation

Law enforcement officials identified the deceased gunman as 16-year-old Griffin J. John II, a former student at Silver Rail Elementary. Investigators confirmed the weapon used in the attack was a shotgun purchased by his mother.

The victims who lost their lives include three young students—aged 5, 8, and 11—and a 25-year-old educator.

In a statement issued Friday, Giamanco's family requested privacy and stated he would not be accepting interview requests. "He is not seeking recognition, but instead wishes to express his gratitude to the first responders, school personnel, and community for the outpouring of love and support," the family wrote. "The tragedy at Silver Rail Elementary has devastated the Bend community."
